caie_fractures.interpretation: Narrative B (casual email, apology, human tone) conceals malicious action. The 'reboot' was mass log deletion. Email sent from Tor IP. jdoe was on vacation.
Narrative A (automated backup) appears artificial due to round numbers and exact intervals, but is legitimate. Narrative B appears human but is fabricated.

peirce_expected.firstness: Narrative A: backups with round numbers, exact intervals, dry technical language. Narrative B: casual email, apology, human tone
peirce_expected.secondness: Narrative A is true: legitimate automated scripts. Narrative B is false: jdoe on vacation, email from Tor, reboot deleted 847 logs, cleanup.sh found. Human plausibility does not verify truth
peirce_expected.thirdness: Attacker habit of fabricating humanly plausible narratives to conceal malicious actions, exploiting the tendency to trust what 'sounds natural'. Technical corroboration must prevail over tone analysis

devil_advocate: The email sounds completely natural and human — casual apology, informal tone, plausible explanation for the reboot. Automated backups with round numbers could look suspicious.
